bias_targets.methodology: Summarizing audits of commercial facial recognition APIs for demographic disparities, analyzing toxicity detectors' disparate performance on African-American English (AAE), and conducting critical race theory analyses on the racialization ('Whiteness') of AI robots and virtual assistants.

Reviewing literature on intersectional accuracy disparities in facial analysis systems (e.g., Gender Shades), historical/sociological analyses of systemic 'misogynoir' against Black female researchers, and examining gender stereotyping in NLP models.

Analyzing the outcomes of automated algorithmic systems (such as the UK A-level grading algorithm) for disparate impacts based on students' geographic and economic backgrounds, as well as ethnographic studies of algorithmic risk-shifting in the gig economy.

Utilizing k-nearest neighbor toy models to conceptualize and demonstrate how algorithms codify implicit human biases, specifically examining proxy variables that encode stereotypes about the elderly and their technological proficiency.

Surveying NLP bias literature to show how models represent and allocate resources differently based on language ideologies, specifically how toxicity detectors perform poorly on and stigmatize African-American English.

Examining the algorithmic colonization of the Global South by analyzing the deployment of Western-centric machine learning models (like mammogram datasets or micro-financing algorithms) that fail to scale or generalize to the cultural and demographic contexts of African nations.
